title: Week 2 Practice: Percent Change, Discounts, and Mixtures
description: Use this set to drill changing bases, discounts, and part-plus-part mixture equations.

questions.question: A price rises from 200 to 250. What is the percent increase?
A 600-peso item is discounted by 15%. What is the sale price?
questions.explanation: Discount is $0.15(600)=90$, so new price is $600-90=510$.

questions.question: A value rises by 20% and then falls by 20%. Starting from 100, what is the final value?
questions.explanation: After the rise: 120. After a 20% decrease on 120: $120-24=96$.

questions.question: A class score drops from 84 to 63. What is the percent decrease?
In a mixture problem, the final concentration must lie between the starting concentrations.
questions.explanation: A weighted average stays between the original values.

questions.question: A 30% discount means subtract 30 pesos.
questions.explanation: A discount is 30% of the original price, not 30 units.

questions.question: How many liters of 10% solution must be added to 5 liters of 40% solution to make a 25% solution?
An item is marked up 25% from cost and sells for 500 pesos. What was the original cost?
